title: Completion accepts a self-asserted second-review flag without a distinct reviewer attestation
observed_behavior: For an achieved high-risk row, validation checks only that second_review_status equals the literal string complete. It does not load a second-review evidence artifact, compare first and second reviewer identities, bind the attestation to the current file hash, or prove that every P0/P1 finding received an independent disposition. A direct probe set reviewer and second-review status on one synthetic row and strict validation returned an empty finding list. The coordinator also twice assigned the original reviewer identity as its own second reviewer before manual identity comparison caught the conflicts.
expected_invariant: Strict completion must derive independent-review completion from a current hash-bound attestation by a reviewer identity distinct from the first pass, and every high-risk achieved file plus every P0/P1 finding must have machine-verifiable independent evidence and disposition.
root_cause: Independent review is represented as an uncorroborated mutable field inside the first-pass coverage row; the ledger has no separate attestation schema, identity comparison, current-hash join, or P0/P1 finding-coverage check.
failure_scenario: A first-pass worker or coordinator writes second_review_status=complete without a second agent, or mistakenly reassigns the same canonical agent under a different task label. The strict coverage gate reports completion even though the required independent review never occurred.
evidence: repository_audit_ledger.py lines 1623-1626 validates only the enum and literal complete value for high-risk achieved rows.
The focused test only proves pending is rejected; it supplies no second artifact or distinct identity for complete.
A bundled-Python synthetic high-risk row with reviewer=same-first-pass-reviewer and second_review_status=complete returned validation_findings(..., require_complete=True) == [].

AUDIT-ERR-COORD-030 and AUDIT-ERR-COORD-034 document two real coordination assignments where the same canonical first-pass agent was initially selected for second review; only manual inspection prevented false attestation.
existing_safeguards: High-risk rows have a second_review_status field and strict completion rejects pending.
Worker reports carry reviewer prose and hashes.
Coordinator manually compares identities and can reject a self-review.
safeguard_gap: None of those facts are joined or enforced by the machine proof gate; task labels and free-form reviewer strings can be mistaken for independence.
tests_present: test_validation_rejects_missing_duplicate_and_false_terminal_claims checks that pending fails for one high-risk row.
tests_missing: High-risk file coverage derived from attestations rather than a row flag.
Every P0/P1 finding independently attested with a matching current disposition.
Same canonical agent under different task labels rejected.
recommended_remediation: Add a separate independent-attestation JSONL schema and loader. Require exact path/hash/worker joins, first-reviewer equality, a distinct canonical second reviewer, nonempty evidence, and finding-disposition mappings. Derive second_review_status from valid attestations during deterministic matrix reconstruction, and make strict completion reject any high-risk achieved row or P0/P1 finding without current independent evidence.
remediation_risk: medium: existing rows that self-assert complete must be migrated to explicit attestations, reviewer identity normalization must avoid false equivalence/inequivalence, and disputed second-review dispositions must block rather than be silently overwritten
validation_rung: Adversarial audit-ledger unit tests and isolated Git flows for self-review, distinct review, stale hash, duplicate/missing attestations, P1 coverage/disagreement, fragment reconstruction, and strict completion; then independent rereview of the hardened tool itself.
prior_audit_relationship: New proof-gate defect discovered while reconciling W10/W02 reviewer identities after the first W11 hardening pass; no prior finding enforced reviewer independence as machine evidence.

title: The first-pass loader silently excludes eight valid prior-audit semantic reviews
observed_behavior: The review loader scans only worker-*-review.jsonl. The established prior-production-audit-review.jsonl contains eight current-hash, nonoverlapping semantic review rows, but none are loaded or merged. A direct path census found 8 rows in that fragment, 21 rows in matching worker fragments, and zero overlap; the loader therefore reports only 21 of 29 available first-pass reviews.
expected_invariant: Every authorized first-pass review fragment in the audit pack must be discovered deterministically or rejected explicitly; valid evidence must never disappear solely because its established filename predates a narrowed glob.
root_cause: Independent-attestation hardening narrowed first-pass discovery to a worker-prefixed glob without migrating or explicitly including the pre-existing prior-production audit fragment.
failure_scenario: A baseline rebuild succeeds while silently resetting eight already reviewed paths to pending, understates prior-audit reconciliation, wastes duplicate review effort, and severs the machine coverage ledger from its accompanying reconciliation report.
evidence: prior-production-audit-review.jsonl has eight JSONL records for backend instance, close readiness, pending paths, rename history, backfill, Tauri single-instance guard, and their tests.
PowerShell JSON path comparison returned prior_count=8, worker_count=21, overlap=[]; none of the eight can enter prepare_review_rows through the current loader.
existing_safeguards: Fragment validation checks shape, ownership, hashes, and duplicate paths after a fragment is loaded.
The prior-audit report and JSONL remain present on disk.
safeguard_gap: No inventory declares authorized fragment filenames and no test proves that the established prior-production fragment is included; an unmatched valid fragment is ignored without a diagnostic.
tests_present: Review merge tests cover a worker-99-review.jsonl fragment.
tests_missing: A diagnostic or manifest check for unexpected review-shaped JSONL files that are not loaded.
recommended_remediation: Explicitly include the established prior-production-audit-review.jsonl alongside worker-prefixed first-pass fragments, deduplicate paths through the existing validator, and add a focused loader regression test. Longer term, use a declared fragment manifest or schema-based discovery with explicit exclusions.
remediation_risk: low: loader-only change, but duplicate-path validation must remain active and independent/self-recheck artifacts must stay excluded
validation_rung: Focused loader test, full audit-ledger unit suite, lint, compile, deterministic baseline rebuild, and independent rereview at frozen hashes.
prior_audit_relationship: New audit-infrastructure defect found during the schema-v2 migration; the omitted evidence itself comes from the already completed prior production audit reconciliation.

title: Tracked files absent from a dirty worktree cannot be inventoried from their Git blobs
observed_behavior: The live repository has 6,061 tracked paths, of which 76 are absent from the shared worktree because of unrelated user-owned deletions (50 release packet JSON files and 26 generated summaries). build_rows assigns absent paths empty content hashes and null line counts, while current_content_findings unconditionally rejects them as missing. A non-mutating reconstruction therefore returned 88 findings and could not apply any review fragments, even though Git's index still contains exact blob IDs and bytes for all 76 paths.
expected_invariant: The audit must cover every tracked path without restoring or overwriting unrelated user changes. When a tracked worktree file is absent, the ledger should explicitly bind inventory and review to the current Git index blob, retain provenance, and detect later index drift.
root_cause: Coverage freshness assumes every tracked path has a regular worktree file and never falls back to the already collected git ls-files --stage blob identity or git cat-file content.
failure_scenario: Any unrelated deletion in a shared dirty worktree blocks the entire deterministic baseline rebuild. The auditor must either violate the preserve-user-changes rule by restoring files or leave the tracked universe incomplete, so exhaustive completion becomes impossible despite recoverable immutable Git content.
evidence: Exact census: git ls-files returned 6,061 paths; Test-Path found 76 absent, grouped as docs=26 and ops=50.
git ls-files --stage still provides a blob hash for the missing paths.
prepare_review_rows built 6,064 candidate rows but emitted a missing-worktree finding for every absent tracked file and applied zero achieved rows.
existing_safeguards: The tool records Git blob hashes for tracked paths.
Missing worktree files currently fail closed rather than being marked reviewed.
safeguard_gap: The recorded blob identity is not used to retrieve content, calculate SHA-256/line counts, classify the file, or validate freshness when the worktree copy is absent; provenance cannot express index-blob review.
tests_present: Stale worktree content prevents review merge.
Tracked and untracked path coverage is tested with present files.
tests_missing: Tracked file deleted from worktree but present in the Git index.
Index-blob SHA-256, line-count, classification, provenance, and later index-drift validation.
recommended_remediation: For absent tracked paths with a stage-0 blob, read bytes via git cat-file blob, calculate inventory metadata from those bytes, set explicit content_source=git_index_blob, and make freshness compare both the recorded blob ID and SHA-256 against current index content. Continue rejecting absent untracked/audit-owned files and unresolved index states.
remediation_risk: medium: blob reads must be byte-safe and bounded, merge-conflict stages must not be mistaken for stage 0, and reviewers must read the same index bytes identified by the ledger rather than silently substituting HEAD or worktree content
validation_rung: Isolated temporary-Git tests for absent tracked text/binary files and index drift, full audit-ledger suite, lint, compile, live schema reconstruction, and independent rereview at frozen hashes.
prior_audit_relationship: New infrastructure defect exposed by preserving the user's pre-existing dirty worktree during the exhaustive audit.

title: Baseline prose always reports zero completed reviews after reviewed rows are merged
observed_behavior: baseline_markdown emits the hard-coded statement '0 complete; all reviewable rows pending' for every row set. write_outputs and merge_review_ledgers both call it after applying current review fragments, so BASELINE.md continues claiming zero progress even when the JSONL/CSV contain achieved rows. The focused test positively requires the stale literal instead of exercising mixed statuses.
expected_invariant: Every generated human-readable coverage mirror must deterministically summarize the statuses in the same row set as its JSONL/CSV source without converting inventory into semantic-review claims.
root_cause: Initialization wording from the original pending-only baseline was left hard-coded after write_outputs was changed to reconstruct and apply current review fragments.
failure_scenario: Operators and later agents read BASELINE.md after a valid merge and conclude no files were reviewed, duplicate completed work, or distrust the JSONL/Markdown mirror relationship even though the matrix is current.
evidence: baseline_markdown appends a literal zero-complete/all-pending line and never counts review_status.
write_outputs passes prepared rows with fragment overrides to baseline_markdown.
test_baseline_does_not_claim_semantic_review asserts the hard-coded literal using a row with no review_status field.
existing_safeguards: COVERAGE_MATRIX.jsonl and CSV retain per-row review_status.
Strict checks compare BASELINE.md bytes to baseline_markdown output.
safeguard_gap: The byte-consistency check reproduces the same wrong summary, so it proves determinism but not truthful aggregation.
tests_present: A pending-only baseline test prevents automated inventory from claiming semantic review.
tests_missing: Mixed pending/achieved/blocked status counts in BASELINE.md.
recommended_remediation: Compute achieved, blocked, and open counts from review_status in the supplied rows, retain the inventory-not-semantic-review caveat, and replace the literal test with pending-only plus mixed-status assertions.
remediation_risk: low: generated audit prose and focused tests only; JSONL status authority is unchanged
validation_rung: Focused baseline aggregation tests, full audit-ledger suite, Ruff, py_compile, live deterministic reconstruction, and exact-hash independent rereview.
prior_audit_relationship: New mirror-accuracy defect found during schema-v2 reconstruction before the first reviewed baseline was published.

title: Review merges omit BASELINE.md from the atomic coverage artifact transaction
observed_behavior: merge_review_ledgers atomically replaces only COVERAGE_MATRIX.jsonl and COVERAGE_MATRIX.csv. Once baseline progress became row-derived, the existing strict fixture immediately failed because BASELINE.md retained the pre-merge counts. Before that change, the hard-coded zero-progress text made the omitted mirror appear current by coincidence.
expected_invariant: Every mutation of the coverage row set must publish JSONL, CSV, and BASELINE.md from the same rows, HEAD, and branch in one rollback-capable artifact transaction.
root_cause: The review-merge writer retained a two-file output list after BASELINE.md became a semantic mirror of merged row state; only write_outputs included all three files.
failure_scenario: A successful review merge advances machine rows while the primary human handoff remains stale. Strict check fails, or an operator consumes the stale baseline between merge and a later write, producing contradictory coverage evidence.
evidence: merge_review_ledgers passes exactly matrix_path and COVERAGE_MATRIX.csv to atomic_write_text_set.
check_outputs independently requires BASELINE.md to equal baseline_markdown(current rows).
The 33-test run failed only the strict mirror test with 'BASELINE.md is missing or stale relative to the current coverage generation' after row-derived counts were enabled.
existing_safeguards: The JSONL and CSV are published together with rollback.
Strict check detects a stale baseline after the fact.
write_outputs already publishes all three mirrors.
safeguard_gap: Detection occurs after merge, and the merge transaction itself cannot keep the Markdown mirror consistent or roll it back with the machine files.
tests_present: Artifact-set rollback test for replacement failure.
tests_missing: Successful review merge updates row-derived BASELINE.md in the same transaction.
Rollback restores all three coverage mirrors if the third replacement fails.
recommended_remediation: Resolve branch and HEAD during merge_review_ledgers, add BASELINE.md/baseline_markdown(rows) as the third atomic output, and extend transaction tests to cover third-file failure if feasible.
remediation_risk: low to medium: generated audit artifacts only, but transaction ordering and rollback must preserve all prior versions on failure
validation_rung: Focused strict merge/mirror and three-file rollback tests, full audit-ledger suite, Ruff, py_compile, live reconstruction, and exact-hash independent rereview.
prior_audit_relationship: New artifact-set omission exposed when SR-008 made baseline status content depend on merged rows.
